title: Introduce contextual failure scorer and hierarchical sample adapter
author: Aditi Suresh
release_notes: Add contextual failure scoring and hierarchical sampling adapter for CI; non-breaking behavioral change to eval sampling (opt-in).
description:
Motivation:
We observe noisy CI failures on large prompt sets where uniformly sampling recent failures overweights semantically redundant failure clusters. This PR introduces a lightweight contextual failure scorer and a hierarchical sampling adapter that together produce a more diverse, failure-focused sample portfolio for regression checks and smoke-evals. The goal is to keep CI sensitivity to real regressions while reducing spurious churn from repeated near-duplicates.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Adds a contextual failure scorer that assigns a continuous failure weight to examples by combining historical failure frequency, recent delta magnitude, and semantic distinctiveness relative to other failing prompts (cosine similarity over embeddings). Scoring is configurable via three tunable factors: history_weight, delta_weight, novelty_weight.
- Introduces a hierarchical sampler (eval_harness.sampling.HierarchicalFailureSampler) which: (1) clusters candidate failures using a cheap locality-sensitive hashing pass, (2) selects cluster representatives by highest failure score, and (3) fills remaining budget with diversity-aware draws. The sampler exposes deterministic seeding for reproducible CI runs.
- Adds a CI hook (ci/hooks/contextual_failure_sampler.py) to integrate the sampler into the prompt-set regression job: the hook replaces the legacy uniform failure sampler when the repository config toggles contextual_sampling: true. The hook emits telemetry (chosen_prompt_ids, cluster_id, score_components) to the eval event stream.
- Adds unit and integration tests and a small RFD doc describing configuration knobs and intended operational behavior.

- [x] Core scorer implementation with pluggable embedding provider interface
- [x] Hierarchical sampler implementation with LSH pre-cluster step

- [x] Docs: rfd and examples for tuning parameters
- [x] Backwards-compatibility: sampler is opt-in; default behavior unchanged

Design notes and rationale:
- We avoid full pairwise similarity (O(n^2)) by using a two-pass approach: LSH bucketization followed by exact similarity only inside buckets. This keeps runtime and memory bounded for large prompt sets (tens of thousands).
- The scorer is intentionally additive and normalized so teams can reason about weight contributions and disable components independently. Example: set novelty_weight=0 to replicate frequency-only behavior.
- The sampler preserves determinism via an explicit seed applied to both LSH hashing and representative selection; this is critical for reproducible CI blames.

Testing and CI behavior observed during review cycle:
- Initial CI run (full unit + integration matrix) hit a flaky test in tests/test_hierarchical_sampler.py due to an underspecified fixture (ordering of LSH buckets).
- I pushed a fix that stabilizes bucket ordering and added a table-driven test that verifies deterministic outputs for a given seed.
- After rerun, CI passed all checks (unit, linters, mypy). Coverage delta: +1.2% in sampling area.

Review highlights and conversation (single-string list summarizing thread):
- Marco Li: "Nice approach. Please add a brief explanation of tradeoffs in the RFD and include default parameter recommendations for small vs large prompt sets."
- Aditi (author): "Added an RFD and default presets (small/medium/large) in docs; included rationale for LSH bucket size and seed strategy."
- Priya Nandan: "Tests look good; can we add an e2e smoke test hooked into the CI regression job to validate telemetry format?"
- Aditi: "Added a lightweight e2e test that runs the hook against a 200-sample fixture and asserts telemetry keys. Kept it behind a -quick tag to limit runtime in presubmits."
- Owen Carter: "Consider exposing a metric that tracks inter-cluster duplicate rate over time so we can detect when our novelty component is under- or over-weighting."
- Aditi: "Filed ENG-1210 to track productizing that metric; added TODO in RFD."

Operational notes and rolling out: 
- Default behavior unchanged: repository must opt-in by setting contextual_sampling: true in eval-config.yaml.
- The sampler is guarded behind a feature flag to allow gradual rollout to large monorepos.
- Telemetry includes score breakdown which teams can export to dashboards for tuning.

Backward compatibility and safety: 
- No breaking API changes. The new scorer implements the existing Scorer interface. Sampler is optional.
- Config defaults maintain current uniform sampling behavior.
- Unit/integration tests ensure the legacy path remains exercised.

Performance: 
- Microbenchmarking with 50k prompt set: LSH pre-clustering + representative selection completes ~2.1s vs naive similarity ~14s on CI runners (median). Memory use reduced significantly by avoiding full matrix materialization.

Merge:
- After approvals from Marco and Priya and green CI, this PR was squash-merged into main (merge method: squash) on 2026-01-26.

References and related work:
- Related Linear tasks: ENG-1184 (reduce noisy regression churn), ENG-1210 (operational duplicate-rate metric)
- Prior art: previous failure-sampler implementations in repo (legacy uniform sampler) and notes in docs/rfd/2024-08-sampler-postmortem.md

How to use (short example):
1) In eval-config.yaml: contextual_sampling: true
2) Optional tuning: contextual_scoring: {history_weight: 0.6, delta_weight: 0.3, novelty_weight: 0.1} and sampler_presets: {small, medium, large}
3) Run the regression job and inspect eval.telemetry.contextual_sampler.* for chosen_prompt_ids and cluster metadata.

If anything needs to be rolled back quickly we can flip contextual_sampling: false — no migrations required.
